title: ipconfig
description: Display full TCP/IP configuration for all network adapters.
output:
Ethernet adapter Ethernet0:
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 10.0.0.15
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . : 10.0.0.1
notes: 'ipconfig /flushdns' clears the local DNS resolver cache — useful after a suspected DNS-poisoning incident.

title: tasklist
description: List all currently running processes, similar to Task Manager's process tab.
notes: '/svc' shows which services run inside each host process (useful for svchost.exe triage).

title: taskkill
description: Terminate a process by PID or image name. /F forces termination.
output: SUCCESS: The process "notepad.exe" has been terminated.
notes: /T also kills the entire child-process tree.

title: netstat
description: Show active connections and listening ports, with -o showing the owning PID.
notes: Cross-reference the PID column with 'tasklist' to identify the responsible process.

title: shutdown
description: Shut down, restart, log off, or hibernate the local or a remote computer.
notes: /a aborts a pending shutdown before the timer expires.

title: ping
description: Send ICMP echo requests to test reachability and latency.
notes: -t pings continuously until stopped with Ctrl+C.

title: tracert
description: Trace the route packets take to a destination host (Windows equivalent of traceroute).
notes: -d skips reverse DNS lookups, speeding up the trace considerably.

title: nslookup
description: Query DNS servers interactively or in batch mode.
output: example.com MX preference = 10, mail exchanger = mail.example.com
notes: Run 'nslookup' with no arguments to enter interactive mode against the default DNS server.

title: systeminfo
description: Display detailed OS configuration, including patch level, hotfixes and boot time.
notes: Cross-check the hotfix list against known CVEs during a patch-compliance review.

title: hostname
description: Print the computer's network name.
notes: Combine with 'whoami' when documenting evidence during an IR engagement.

title: whoami
description: Display the current user, and with /all their SID, groups, and privileges.
output:
PRIVILEGES INFORMATION
SeDebugPrivilege  Debug programs  Disabled
notes: SeDebugPrivilege and SeImpersonatePrivilege being enabled are common privilege-escalation footholds.

title: wmic
description: Query WMI from the command line for system, process, and hardware information (deprecated since Win10 21H1 in favor of PowerShell).
example: wmic process where name="notepad.exe" get processid
notes: Deprecated but still present on many hosts — attackers use it for living-off-the-land recon.

title: gpupdate
description: Refresh local and Active Directory Group Policy settings immediately.
output: Computer Policy update has completed successfully.
notes: 'gpresult /r' shows which policies are actually applied to the current session.

title: sfc
description: Scan and repair protected system files against the component store.
output: Windows Resource Protection found corrupt files and successfully repaired them.
notes: Run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' first if sfc itself reports it cannot repair files.

title: dism
description: Servicing tool for mounting, repairing and configuring Windows images.
notes: Often run before sfc /scannow when the component store itself is damaged.

title: net user
description: Manage local user accounts — create, modify, delete, view.
notes: Legacy tool; PowerShell's Get-LocalUser/New-LocalUser are the modern equivalent.

title: net localgroup
description: View or modify local group membership.
notes: Unexpected members of the local Administrators group are a common IR finding.

title: net share
description: List, create or delete SMB network shares.
output:
Share name  Resource   Remark
C$          C:\        Default share
notes: Default administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$) are frequently abused for lateral movement.

title: diskpart
description: Interactive command-line disk partitioning utility.
output:
Disk ### Status Size
Disk 0 Online 238 GB
notes: Type 'list disk' then 'select disk N' before any destructive operation — double-check the disk number.

title: chkdsk
description: Check a disk for filesystem errors and, with /f, fix them.
notes: /r additionally locates bad sectors and recovers readable information; requires a reboot on the system volume.

title: schtasks
description: View, create or delete scheduled tasks from the command line.
output: SUCCESS: The scheduled task "Backup" has successfully been created.
notes: Attacker-created scheduled tasks are a common persistence mechanism — audit /query /fo LIST /v regularly.

title: dir
description: List directory contents. /a shows hidden files, /s recurses subdirectories.
notes: '/o:d' sorts by date, handy for finding recently dropped files during triage.

title: copy / xcopy / robocopy
description: Copy files/folders; robocopy is the modern, resumable, multithreaded option.
notes: /MIR mirrors the source, deleting files at the destination that no longer exist at the source — use with care.

title: del / erase
description: Delete one or more files. /f forces deletion of read-only files, /q suppresses prompts.
notes: Deleted files bypass the Recycle Bin when removed from the command line.

title: attrib
description: View or change file attributes: hidden, system, read-only, archive.
notes: Malware commonly sets +h +s on dropped files to hide them from a casual Explorer view.

title: icacls
description: View or modify NTFS permissions (ACLs) on files and folders.
notes: icacls C:\path /reset restores inherited permissions, useful for undoing a misconfiguration.

title: reg
description: Read or modify the Windows Registry from the command line.
notes: The Run/RunOnce keys are among the most common persistence locations to check first.

title: sc
description: Query or configure Windows services from the command line (Service Controller).
example: sc query state= all | findstr RUNNING
notes: 'sc qc svcname' shows the service's binary path — check for unexpected paths pointing outside System32.

title: netsh
description: Configure networking components: firewall, interfaces, WLAN profiles.
example: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="BlockTelnet" dir=in action=block protocol=TCP localport=23
notes: 'netsh wlan show profiles key=clear' reveals saved Wi-Fi passwords in cleartext.

title: route
description: Display or modify the local IP routing table.
notes: Unexplained static routes can indicate a compromised host redirecting traffic.

title: arp
description: Display or modify the local ARP cache mapping IPs to MAC addresses.
notes: Sudden ARP-cache changes to the gateway entry can indicate ARP spoofing/MITM.

title: type
description: Display the contents of a text file (Windows equivalent of cat).
notes: Unexpected entries in the hosts file are a classic sign of DNS-hijacking malware.

title: findstr
description: Search for text patterns in files, similar to grep. /s recurses, /i ignores case.
notes: /n shows line numbers; /r enables basic regular expressions.

title: cipher
description: Manage EFS encryption; the /w switch securely wipes free space on a volume.
notes: Useful for confirming deleted-file remnants have been overwritten during sanitization.

title: certutil
description: Manage certificates, and (unofficially) hash files or decode base64 — no dedicated tool needed.
notes: Attackers abuse certutil -urlcache/-decode as a living-off-the-land downloader — always review its use.

title: robocopy
description: See 'copy / xcopy / robocopy' above — listed separately as it is frequently searched on its own.
notes: /XA:H excludes hidden files; /R:1 limits retry attempts on locked files to 1.

title: wevtutil
description: Query and manage Windows Event Logs directly from the command line.
notes: Event ID 4625 = failed logon; 4624 = successful logon — foundational for brute-force hunting.

title: takeown
description: Take ownership of a file or folder that the current user lacks permission to access.
output: SUCCESS: The file (or folder) now owned by user.
notes: Often paired with icacls to grant full control after regaining ownership.

title: driverquery
description: List all installed device drivers and their properties.
notes: Unsigned kernel drivers are a red flag worth investigating — a common rootkit vector.

title: msconfig / bcdedit
description: View or modify Boot Configuration Data (boot manager entries, safe-mode options).
notes: bcdedit is command-line only; msconfig provides a GUI over similar boot settings.

title: fsutil
description: Perform low-level filesystem tasks: query volume info, manage NTFS features, reparse points.
output:
Volume Name : OS
File System Name : NTFS
notes: 'fsutil usn readjournal' can help reconstruct recently deleted/renamed files during an investigation.
